case.case_title: Ansalin Fernando v. Sarath Perera, Officer-in-Charge, Police Station, Chilaw and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 18/87, decided on 19 and 30 March 1990

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention of the 6th respondent was lawful and complied with the requirement to be brought before a judge and held only under legal authority.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed the 6th respondent was detained unlawfully without proper detention orders and was not produced before a judge within the required time.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents claimed the 6th respondent was detained under detention orders issued under Emergency Regulations and was produced before a Magistrate on 04.02.87.
key_facts: The 6th respondent was detained from 02.01.87 to 20.02.87, including a period at Kalutara Police Station without a detention order.
A detention order under Regulation 19(2) was obtained on 07.01.87 authorizing detention for 30 days from 06.01.87.
The 6th respondent was produced before a Magistrate on 04.02.87 and remanded for a further period.
No detention order was produced for the period 05.02.87 to 20.02.87 during which the 6th respondent was detained at Kalutara Police Station.
The detention order was found to be illegal as it was based on an offence under Regulation 45 which does not create an offence.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained be brought before a judge and held only under legal authority. The court held that detention without a valid detention order or legal authority is illegal. The detention order must specify the reason and be lawful.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The 6th respondent was detained for a period without a valid detention order and was not informed of the reason for detention. The detention order relied on an invalid offence and was therefore illegal. Detention at Kalutara Police Station without any order was unlawful.
principles_established: Detention must be authorized by a valid legal order and the detainee must be brought before a judge.
Detention orders must specify the reason for detention and be lawful.
Detention without legal authority violates Article 13(2).
precedents_cited: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera (1985) 1 Sri LR 375
Wijewardena v. Zain and Others S.C. Application No. 202/87

outcome.holding: The court held that the detention of the 6th respondent was illegal and violated Article 13(2) due to lack of valid detention orders and failure to inform the detainee of the reason.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The State was ordered to pay compensation and costs.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court's finding that the detention was unlawful because the 6th respondent was held without valid detention orders and not properly brought before a judge, directly leading to the relief granted.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found the detention order illegal as it was based on an invalid offence and that the 6th respondent was detained without authority from 05.02.87 to 20.02.87, violating Article 13(2).
